indicators.flag: A customer in the maritime industry transports commodities of concern and uses trade corridors known to serve as possible transshipment points21 for exports to Russia and Belarus.
indicators.red_flag: Maritime-industry customer moving commodities-of-concern via known transshipment corridors
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D15 (Trade-finance / customs / shipping & logistics data), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: The nature of a customer’s underlying business (specifically military or government-related work), type of service(s) or product(s) offered, and geographical presence pose additional risks of unintentional involvement in the evasion of export controls for Russia and Belarus.
indicators.red_flag: Military/government-linked business profile in export-control-evasion-risk geography
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D8 (KYC / CDD & beneficial-ownership data), not currently held → source data first.

build_logic.logic: Flag a personal account whose inflow volume or wealth velocity is inconsistent with the customer's declared income, occupation, or stated source of funds, escalating when large credits lack a plausible origin for the customer's profile.
build_logic.window: rolling 90 days vs declared income profile
build_logic.source: personal deposit ledger joined to onboarding income/occupation KYC data
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert â AML analyst review gate

indicators.flag: A customer acquires new vessels for no apparent economic or business purpose or for use in shipping corridors involving one or more of the identified transshipment countries.
indicators.red_flag: No-economic-purpose vessel acquisition into transshipment-corridor use
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D16 (Maritime / vessel data (AIS & registries)), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: A customer purchases or sells vessels or other properties and goods identified as having been involved with or being blocked property under U.S. or partner country sanctions.
indicators.red_flag: Trade in vessels/goods flagged as sanctions-blocked property
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C18 (Sanctions / watchlist screening).

indicators.flag: Transactions involving entities with little to no web presence.
indicators.red_flag: Counterparty with no web/OSINT footprint
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C19 (Adverse-media / OSINT & web-presence verification); data D13.

indicators.flag: Transactions involving a change in shipments or payments that were previously scheduled to go to Russia or Belarus, or a company located in Russia or Belarus, but that are now going to a different country/company.
indicators.red_flag: Re-routed shipment/payment away from Russia/Belarus to a substitute destination (evasion diversion)
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C20 (Cross-border / high-risk-jurisdiction & corridor anomaly detection).

indicators.flag: Transactions involving payments being made from entities located in third-party countries not otherwise involved with the transactions and known to be a potential transshipment point for exports to Russia and Belarus.
indicators.red_flag: Payment from unrelated third-party transshipment-hub entity
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C20 (Cross-border / high-risk-jurisdiction & corridor anomaly detection).

indicators.flag: Last-minute changes to transactions associated with an originator or beneficiary located in Russia or Belarus.
indicators.red_flag: Last-minute party/route change on a Russia/Belarus originator-beneficiary leg
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C20 (Cross-border / high-risk-jurisdiction & corridor anomaly detection).

indicators.flag: Parties to transactions with addresses that do not appear consistent with the business or are otherwise problematic (e.g., either the physical address does not exist, or it is residential).
indicators.red_flag: Counterparty address inconsistent with business (nonexistent/residential)
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C13 (Account-opening / KYC risk profiling).

indicators.flag: Transactions involving consolidated shipments of luxury goods that previously would have been destined for Russia or Belarus, but are now destined for a transshipment country or a country without restrictions on exports/re-exports to Russia or Belarus.
indicators.red_flag: Re-routed consolidated luxury-goods shipment to a non-restricted transshipment destination
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C20 (Cross-border / high-risk-jurisdiction & corridor anomaly detection).

indicators.flag: Rapid shifts to new purchasers of transactions involving restricted luxury goods.
indicators.red_flag: Rapid purchaser-substitution on restricted luxury-goods deals
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C1 (Customer-profile / out-of-pattern transaction monitoring); data D1.

indicators.flag: Transactions involving freight-forwarding firms22 that are also listed as the product’s final end customer, especially items going to traditional Russian transshipment hubs.
indicators.red_flag: Freight-forwarder named as final end-customer (end-user obfuscation)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D15 (Trade-finance / customs / shipping & logistics data), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: Transactions associated with atypical shipping routes for a product and destination.
indicators.red_flag: Atypical shipping route for the product/destination pair
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D15 (Trade-finance / customs / shipping & logistics data), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: Transactions involving entities whose website or business registration states the entities work on “special purpose projects.”23
indicators.red_flag: Counterparty self-describing “special purpose projects” (military-use designation)
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C19 (Adverse-media / OSINT & web-presence verification); data D13.

indicators.flag: Transactions involving companies that display a certificate from the Federal Security Service of the Russian Federation (FSB RF), which allows these companies to work on projects classified as a state secret.
indicators.red_flag: Counterparty advertising FSB-RF state-secret certification
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C19 (Adverse-media / OSINT & web-presence verification); data D13.

indicators.flag: Transactions involving companies that are physically co-located with or have shared ownership with an entity on the BIS Entity List25 or the Department of the Treasury’s Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List.
indicators.red_flag: Co-location / shared ownership with a BIS Entity List or SDN entity
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D11 (Sanctions / watchlist & regulator-action data), not currently held → source data first.

build_logic.logic: Flag an entity exhibiting shell or front-company markers â opaque or circular beneficial ownership, shared registered addresses or directors, recent incorporation with no observable operations â escalating when nominees or addresses recur across a cluster of related entities.
build_logic.window: rolling 90 days over the ownership/address graph
build_logic.source: corporate registry + KYC beneficial-ownership records + entity-resolution graph
build_logic.route: Tier-2 network alert â AML investigations gate

indicators.flag: New or existing accounts and transactions by individuals with previous convictions for violating U.S. export control laws, particularly if appearing to involve export and import activities or services.
indicators.red_flag: Account holder with prior export-control-violation convictions in export/import activity
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C13 (Account-opening / KYC risk profiling).

indicators.flag: When combined with other derogatory information, large dollar or volume purchases, including through the use of business credit cards, of items designated as EAR99 (or large volume or dollar purchases at wholesale electrical/industrial merchants, electrical parts and equipment providers, or electronic parts providers), in the United States or abroad, especially if paired with purchases at shipping companies.
indicators.red_flag: Large card/volume EAR99 buys at electronics/industrial merchants paired with shipping-company spend
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D4 (Card & merchant-category (MCC) transaction data), not currently held → source data first.

build_logic.logic: Flag a card or account whose merchant-category spend distribution shifts toward high-risk or atypical MCCs for the customer's segment, escalating when spend concentrates in cash-equivalent categories such as gift cards, prepaid, or money-services merchants.
build_logic.window: rolling 60 days vs segment MCC baseline
build_logic.source: card authorization/settlement feed enriched with MCC reference
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert â AML analyst review gate

indicators.flag: Companies or individuals with links to Russian state-owned corporations (including shared ownership, as well as branches of, subsidiaries of, or shareholders in such state-owned corporations) involved in export-related transactions or the provision of export-related services.
indicators.red_flag: Ownership links to Russian state-owned corporations on export-related activity
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D8 (KYC / CDD & beneficial-ownership data), not currently held → source data first.

build_logic.logic: Flag an entity exhibiting shell or front-company markers â opaque or circular beneficial ownership, shared registered addresses or directors, recent incorporation with no observable operations â escalating when nominees or addresses recur across a cluster of related entities.
build_logic.window: rolling 90 days over the ownership/address graph
build_logic.source: corporate registry + KYC beneficial-ownership records + entity-resolution graph
build_logic.route: Tier-2 network alert â AML investigations gate

indicators.flag: Export transactions identified through correspondent banking activities involving non- U.S. parties that have shared owners or addresses with Russian state-owned entities or designated companies.
indicators.red_flag: Correspondent-banking export leg sharing owners/addresses with Russian state-owned or designated entities
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C20 (Cross-border / high-risk-jurisdiction & corridor anomaly detection).

indicators.flag: Use of business checking or foreign exchange accounts by U.S.-based merchants involved in the import and export of electronic equipment where transactions are conducted with third- country-based electronics and aerospace firms that also have offices in Russia or Belarus.
indicators.red_flag: US electronics import/export merchant transacting with third-country firms holding Russia/Belarus offices
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C20 (Cross-border / high-risk-jurisdiction & corridor anomaly detection).

indicators.flag: Transactions identified through correspondent banking activities connected to Russian petroleum-related firms or firms that resell electronics and other similar items to Russian firms.
indicators.red_flag: Correspondent-banking activity tied to Russian petroleum firms or electronics-reseller pass-through
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C20 (Cross-border / high-risk-jurisdiction & corridor anomaly detection).
